title: Dataset-fingerprint-driven quant defaults with shadow calibration and staged rollout
creator: Asha Patel
description: Create per-model default quantization profiles (FP8/INT8 and mixed hybrid options) that are selected automatically based on a lightweight dataset fingerprint and workload characteristics. Production rollout uses a staged shadow calibration pipeline to validate accuracy regressions before enabling defaults for live traffic.
background: The model catalog currently lists manual quant recommendations but lacks an automated, workload-aware default selection mechanism. Customers and SRE teams have reported surprising regressions when a blanket INT8 profile is applied to models with skewed token distributions. We need a system that recommends safe defaults and validates them against representative workloads without exposing users to immediate risk.
proposed_solution: Compute a compact fingerprint per model ingest using a small representative prompt set and runtime statistics (token length distribution, activation magnitude percentiles, common tokens). Map fingerprints to candidate quant profiles using a nearest-neighbor look-up in a catalog seeded by prior calibrations. For each candidate default, run a shadow calibration using a holdout validation set and a fast evaluator that measures key metrics (perplexity delta, task-specific accuracy, hallucination rate). Only promote defaults after the shadow job passes acceptance thresholds and an automated rollback plan is recorded.
rollout_plan: 1) Implement fingerprint extractor and indexing job (batch) for cataloged models
2) Add catalog table entries for candidate profiles with provenance and confidence bands
3) Build shadow calibration job that runs in a non-serving namespace and reports metrics
4) Create promotion criteria and automated gating in the catalog UI and API
5) Stage rollout: internal models -> beta customers -> public catalog with opt-in -> auto-enable for low-risk models
6) Monitor cost/latency regressions and add automatic fallback to full-precision profiles
acceptance_criteria: Fingerprint extractor runs for 95% of cataloged models within 2 hours of job start
Shadow calibration job produces calibrated INT8/FP8 candidates with confidence bands and stores evaluation artifacts
Automated promotion gate rejects any profile with >0.5% absolute task accuracy drop or >2x hallucination rate increase compared to baseline
API exposes per-model default profile with provenance, confidence score, and link to evaluation summary
Runbook and automated rollback exist and have been exercised in an internal dry-run
risks: Fingerprint may not capture distributional shifts for customer prompts leading to wrong default selection
Shadow calibration compute cost may exceed budget if validation sets are large
Automated gates might be too strict and prevent useful quant savings, or too lax and permit regressions
Telemetry gaps could make it hard to detect slow quality regressions post-promotion
progress_updates: 2025-02-12: Kickoff meeting with ML infra, model-ops, and console teams. Agreed minimal fingerprint schema (len_hist, topk_token_freq, activation_p95).
2025-02-18: Prototype fingerprint extractor committed (PR: github.com/redwood-inference/model-catalog/pull/482). Runs on a sample of 120 models in staging.

2025-02-25: Shadow calibration runner PoC can evaluate INT8/FP8 quant candidates using a 500-prompt eval with mocked metrics. Observed that ~12% of models fail the hallucination gate with current thresholds.
2025-03-03: Design review with PM (Marta Ruiz) and Design (Yuki Tanaka) to finalize UI fields for provenance and confidence. Agreed to expose rollback link and evaluation report PDF.
2025-03-05: Added the promotion gate to the catalog API and wired evaluation artifact storage to the observability bucket (dashboard link created).
qa_notes: QA will run a targeted set of regression tests: semantic similarity (embedding drift), task-specific accuracy for NLU tasks, and hallucination heuristic checks. Plan a canary window of 48 hours and automated rollback if any monitored metric exceeds threshold.
